chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When the people are not waiting for anyone, they are sufficient with one Iqamah."

key_terms.إِقَامَةٍ: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, signaling the start of prayer)

ai.seo_question: When is a single Iqamah sufficient instead of performing both Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: In the context of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration clarifies the juristic distinction between the summoning function of the Adhan and the preparatory function of the Iqamah. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that ritual obligations are tailored to the practical state of the congregation, allowing for flexibility when the community is already assembled and awaiting the Imam's arrival.
